findings.title: Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination. convert (and gifsicle when animation is enabled) opens the output for writing before the input is fully read, and ImageMagick truncates that path immediately. This tempfile is the only copy of the upload, so a large image can become empty or partial before Upload.create_for. The loop also ignores downsize's false return, so a failed conversion is retried against the already truncated file and then handed to create_for. Write to a separate tempfile and replace the original only after a successful non-empty result.

findings.title: Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload by arity, so downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) on line 149 replaces downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) on line 145. The width/height wrapper never exists at runtime. Callers that still use the previous signature — numeric max width and max height, which this pull request does not update anywhere else — now bind the height integer to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError instead of building a widthxheight geometry, so those calls 500.

findings.title: Client size check hardcoded to 10MB for every type
findings.body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each honored their admin setting. It now always uses 10 * 1024. Attachments larger than 10MB are rejected even when max_attachment_size_kb allows them, and attachments between the real attachment limit and 10MB pass the client and fail only on the server. Images are capped at 10MB regardless of max_image_size_kb, so a site that allows larger images cannot upload them from the browser. The 413 handler on line 246 uses the same hardcode, so the dialog always claims the limit is 10240 KB even when the web server or site setting differs.

findings.title: 80% geometry breaks animation and does not enforce the size limit
findings.body: The new call passes "80%" and allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. When that setting is false, downsize_instructions runs convert with a [0] frame selector, so a large animated GIF or multi-page image is permanently flattened to the first frame in the stored original; that setting is about thumbnails, not the upload. When it is true, gifsicle --resize-fit is given "80%", but it requires a pixel size such as 100x100, so it exits non-zero. The failure is ignored, and after five attempts the still-oversized file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway. The loop also does not fail the upload if the file is still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after five 80% passes, so the comment's "reduced to allowed size" guarantee is not enforced for JPEGs or PNGs either.

findings.title: API URL downloads capped at a hardcoded 10MB for all types
findings.body: FileHelper.download's limit changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes to 10.megabytes for every upload type, not only images that will be downsized. Non-image API URL uploads are therefore cut off at 10MB even when max_attachment_size_kb is higher, and they are no longer tied to the attachment setting at all. Image URL uploads also cannot exceed 10MB when max_image_size_kb is configured above that, so the admin setting and the new downscale path disagree.

findings.title: No input size ceiling before repeated ImageMagick runs
findings.body: The browser and the URL-download path are capped at 10MB, but the multipart file branch never checks an upper bound before the downsize loop. The client check is bypassable: any logged-in user can POST a huge image and force up to five ImageMagick convert runs plus ImageOptim inside Scheduler::Defer. A decompression bomb or a multi-hundred-megabyte image is fully decoded on each attempt, which is a CPU and memory exhaustion path. Reject or cap the input before calling downsize, and stop if an attempt does not shrink the file.

findings.title: No tests for downsizing or the new size caps
findings.body: This change alters client limits, URL download limits, and runs a five-iteration ImageMagick downsize before Upload.create_for, but no tests were added. Failures such as in-place conversion, the overwritten downsize signature, attachment versus image limits, a file that stays over max_image_size_kb, and animated GIF handling would not be caught before merge.
